title: Mind the Shift: Decoding Monetary Policy Stance from FOMC Statements with Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2603.14313v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) statements are a major source of monetary-policy information, and even subtle changes in their wording can move global financial markets. A central task is therefore to measure the hawkish--dovish stance conveyed in these texts. Existing approaches typically treat stance detection as a standard classification problem, labeling each statement in isolation. However, the interpretation of monetary-policy communication is inherently relative: market reactions depend not only on the tone of a statement, but also on how that tone shifts across meetings. We introduce Delta-Consistent Scoring (DCS), an annotation-free framework that maps frozen large language model (LLM) representations to continuous stance scores by jointly modeling absolute stance and relative inter-meeting shifts. translated_abstract: 联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）声明是货币政策信息的重要来源，其措辞的细微变化甚至能撬动全球金融市场。因此，衡量这些文本所传达的鹰派—鸽派立场是一项核心任务。现有方法通常将立场检测视为标准的分类问题，对每份声明进行孤立标注。然而，货币政策沟通的解读本质上是相对的：市场反应不仅取决于声明本身的语调，还取决于这一语调在历次会议之间的变化。我们提出了Delta一致评分（DCS），这是一个无需人工标注的框架，通过联合建模绝对立场与会议间的相对变化，将冻结的大型语言模型（LLM）表示映射为连续的立场分数。DCS不依赖人工的鹰派—鸽派标签，而是将连续的会议作为自监督信号的来源。它学习……
tldr: 提出无需人工标注的Delta一致评分（DCS）框架，通过联合建模绝对立场与会议间的立场转变，利用冻结的大语言模型表示从FOMC声明中解码货币政策的鹰派—鸽派立场。
en_tdlr: Proposes Delta-Consistent Scoring (DCS), an annotation-free framework that maps frozen LLM representations to continuous stance scores by jointly modeling absolute hawkish-dovish stance and inter-meeting shifts, decoding monetary policy stance from FOMC statements.
